solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Duke aboard rickety lagoon craft

indicators.note: aboard means being carried inside, so the duke's letter goes within the rest
rickety means shaky and unsound, so the letters of lagoon are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A nobleman sits in an unsteady little boat out on a lagoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rickety' turns LAGOON into GONOLA, and 'aboard' puts D for Duke inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A gondola is a Venetian boat, and craft is a general word for any vessel.

clue.text: Small model supporting half of huge sign

indicators.note: supporting in a down answer means beneath, so the model goes below the half
half of here takes the back half of the word huge

parts.note: the Mini is a small car model

explanation.surface: A little model holds up part of something enormous.
explanation.definitionFit: Gemini, the twins, is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: It's blown by what's blown

parts.note: the instrument is played by breath from the nostrils, and we blow our noses

explanation.walkthrough: The joke is the two senses of blow: playing a wind instrument and clearing your nose.
explanation.definitionFit: A nose flute is a wind instrument played with air from the nostrils, common in Polynesia.

clue.text: One in possession of wand errs periodically

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: Someone holding a magic wand keeps making mistakes.
explanation.walkthrough: Start from the O of 'of' and take alternate letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An owner is a person who possesses something.

clue.text: Upended blue tin 'A' holding no reptiles

indicators.note: upended means turned upside down, which in a down answer reads the letters backwards
holding means containing, so the no goes inside

parts.note: blue means sad
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: An overturned tin labelled A turns out to contain no snakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts NO into SADCANA to give SADNOCANA, and 'Upended' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Anacondas are large constricting snakes of South America, and snakes are reptiles.

clue.text: Sailor replaces litre in Wine Club

indicators.note: replaces says the sailor's letters take the place of the litre's letter in the wine

parts.note: claret is red Bordeaux wine
AB, able seaman, is the usual crossword sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor swaps a litre of something in a wine club, as if it were a drinking society story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wine Club' reads as one society, but Wine gives CLARET and Club is the definition; AB replaces its L.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabaret is a nightclub or restaurant with live entertainment, so it is a kind of club.

clue.text: Runs out of adventures in coastal areas

indicators.note: out of says the runs letter is taken out of the adventures word

parts.note: capers are escapades or adventures
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone runs out of adventures along the coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A cape is a headland jutting into the sea, so capes are pieces of coastline.

clue.text: Marsupial from group overlooking island bird

indicators.note: overlooking in a down answer means sitting above, so the group comes first

parts.note: a band is a group
I is the map abbreviation for island
the coot is a water bird

explanation.surface: A pouched animal comes from a band watching a bird on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: The bandicoot is a small Australian animal that carries its young in a pouch.

clue.text: Brings up first couple having left debts

indicators.note: the first two letters have departed from the debts word

parts.note: arrears are overdue debts

explanation.surface: A newlywed pair raises children after walking out on what they owed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first couple' suggests a married pair, but it means the first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To rear children is to raise or bring them up.

clue.text: Draw the German somersaulting in rows

parts.note: a tie is a drawn game

indicators.note: somersaulting means flipping over, so the German word is reversed

parts.note: der is German for the

explanation.surface: A German tumbles around in lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiered means arranged in layers or ranks one above another.

clue.text: Relatives contacting society member

parts.note: mas are mothers, family relatives
on can mean touching or in contact with

explanation.surface: Family members get in touch with someone who belongs to a society.
explanation.walkthrough: The society is the Freemasons, whose members are called masons.
explanation.definitionFit: A mason is short for Freemason, a member of the fraternal secret society.

clue.text: Extra bit of time after program finale

indicators.note: after says the time word comes following the program and finale pieces

parts.note: an app is a computer program
the finale is the end
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Some additional time is tacked on once a programme has finished.
explanation.definitionFit: An appendage is something added or attached, a supplementary part.

clue.text: Evil UFO is near Barking

indicators.note: barking means mad, so the letters of these words are scrambled

explanation.surface: A sinister flying saucer is said to be hovering close to Barking, a district of east London.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking looks like the London place name, but it is slang for crazy and signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Nefarious means wicked or criminal, a close synonym of the adjective evil.

clue.text: Publication retrospectively links these US sites

indicators.note: retrospectively means looking back, so the found letters are read backwards
links says the answer joins up the words that follow, buried across them

explanation.surface: Looking back, a magazine provides links to American websites.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue is one edition of a magazine or newspaper, a single publication.

clue.text: Fish and game by empty dockyard

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a game

indicators.note: empty means the inside letters of dockyard are removed, leaving only its ends

explanation.surface: Someone fishing and playing a game next to a deserted dockyard.
explanation.definitionFit: The rudd is a freshwater fish of the carp family found in Europe.

clue.text: Old pirate mixed product that might thin beard

indicators.note: mixed means jumbled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An old pirate mixes up something to thin his beard.
explanation.definitionFit: A depilator removes hair, so it could reduce the growth of facial hair.

clue.text: Break up pitted fruit on slate

indicators.note: on means placed after, the fruit following the slate in an across answer

parts.note: to diss is to criticise, as is to slate

indicators.note: pitted means the stone is taken out, here the central letter of the fruit

parts.note: an olive is a stone fruit

explanation.surface: A stoned fruit is placed on a slate before something falls apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitted' removes the middle I of OLIVE, like taking out its stone, to leave OLVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissolve something such as a parliament or partnership is to end it formally.

clue.text: Hairy brute edges to sequoia with short child

indicators.note: the edges of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: squat means short and thick

explanation.surface: A shaggy beast clings to the edges of a giant redwood with a small child.
explanation.definitionFit: Sasquatch, or Bigfoot, is a large ape-like creature of North American folklore covered in hair.

clue.text: Damage vessel inscribed by northern artist

indicators.note: inscribed by means written into, so the northern artist goes inside the vessel

parts.note: a vase is a vessel
Salvador Dali was a surrealist artist

explanation.surface: A vase is defaced by a painter from the north scrawling on it.
explanation.definitionFit: To vandalise is to deliberately wreck or deface property.

clue.text: Teacher puts online where Congress may be recorded?

parts.note: BEd, Bachelor of Education, is a teaching degree, so stands for a teacher
to post is to put up on the internet

explanation.surface: An educator uploads material to the place where the US Congress is documented.
explanation.walkthrough: Congress here is sexual intercourse, not the US legislature; notches on bedposts are the joking record of conquests.
explanation.definitionFit: Lovers traditionally cut notches into the posts of a bed to tally their conquests.

clue.text: Shelter explosive packed with energy

indicators.note: packed with means filled, so the energy letter goes inside the explosive

parts.note: TNT is trinitrotoluene, the explosive
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A shelter with explosives and power stuffed inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tent is a portable canvas shelter used when camping.

clue.text: Joint oddly supple whenever injected by female

indicators.note: injected by here joins the female letter on after the conditional
oddly means take the odd-numbered letters of supple

parts.note: if can mean whenever

explanation.surface: A supple joint gets an injection from a woman, as in a medical treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' sounds anatomical, with supple and injected backing that, but it is slang for a cannabis cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: A spliff is a hand-rolled cannabis cigarette, also called a joint.

clue.text: Layers underpinning boundaries of ancient city

indicators.note: underpinning in a down answer means the layers go beneath
the boundaries of a word are its outer letters

parts.note: hens are layers of eggs

explanation.surface: Rock strata lie beneath the walls of an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Layers' suggests strata, but means birds that lay eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Athens is the capital of Greece, a city with ancient roots.

clue.text: Two exchanging positions in disciplinary board

indicators.note: two letters of the disciplinary word swap their places with each other

parts.note: penal means relating to punishment, disciplinary

explanation.surface: A pair of people swap places on a disciplinary committee.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the E and the A of PENAL gives PANEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A panel is a group of people convened to judge or decide something, like a board.

clue.text: Cold potentially difficult to catch

definitions.meaning: second meaning: quick and agile, so hard to catch

explanation.walkthrough: 'catch' a cold misleads: the second sense is nimbleness, nothing to do with illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Nippy describes bitingly chilly air, and also someone fast and nimble on their feet.

clue.text: Warped statues hot, almost 135 degrees

indicators.note: warped means twisted out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
almost means the word is cut short of its final letter

explanation.surface: Statues bend out of shape in the heat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims HOT to HO, and 'Warped' mixes STATUES with HO.
explanation.definitionFit: On a compass, a bearing of 135 degrees measured clockwise from north points midway between south and east.

clue.text: Rather inclined to take third part off Hollywood actress

indicators.note: the third letter is removed from the actress's name

parts.note: Meryl Streep is a Hollywood actress

explanation.surface: Someone is quite keen to remove part of a film star's role.
explanation.definitionFit: A steep slope rises sharply, so it is markedly sloping.

clue.text: Male sheep mounted by the male gets angry

indicators.note: mounted by in a down answer means with the other piece on top

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
a tup is a ram

explanation.surface: A ram is ridden by a man and becomes cross.
explanation.definitionFit: Het up is an informal phrase for agitated or worked up.

clue.text: Irritable setter's presented with surgeon's charge

parts.note: setter's means the setter is, I'm, the crossword compiler referring to themself
a surgeon's charge is the patient in their care

explanation.surface: A crossword compiler is handed a surgeon's bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' suggests a fee, but here it is a person in someone's care.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone impatient is restless and easily annoyed, short-tempered like an irritable person.

clue.text: Note about rent is nonsense

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the note goes around the tear

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale
a rent is a tear or rip

explanation.surface: A memo concerning the rent is rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' looks like payment for housing but is the past of rend, a tear.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe is stomach lining eaten as food, and by extension worthless talk or rubbish.

clue.text: Quickly move component spinning web?

parts.note: to fly is to move quickly

indicators.note: spinning means turning round, so the component word is read backwards

parts.note: a part is a component

explanation.surface: Swiftly shift a rotating component, as if fixing a machine.
explanation.walkthrough: A spider's web is a trap for flies; the question mark marks the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A spider's web exists to catch insects, so it serves as a trap for flies.

clue.text: Unfortunate bloke represented as 'C' perhaps

indicators.note: says the bloke word, once treated as the answer instructs, is shown as a lone letter C

parts.note: a bloke is a chap, and the answer read as an instruction is applied to that word

explanation.surface: An unlucky man is depicted as a mere letter.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as HAP-LESS: CHAP (bloke) less HAP is C.
explanation.definitionFit: Hapless means lacking luck, from the old word hap meaning chance or fortune.
